scope.method: Exact runner source and existing reporting contract inspection, followed by three bounded synthetic command executions with a cleanup-only fault injection.

prior_closure_preserved.scope_note: CI3 eliminates pipe-EOF waiting in run_command. CI4 concerns its outer environment context teardown before report publication and does not invalidate that source fix.

paths.review_scope: Additional CI4 teardown/report-publication finding only. Prior CI1/CI2/CI3 closure remains intact. No other previously approved source behavior is reopened.

findings.title: Environment teardown failure prevents publication of completed command evidence
findings.trigger: TemporaryDirectory.__exit__ raises OSError/PermissionError while cleaning the isolated test environment, after run_command has returned. The report destination itself remains writable.
findings.impact: main propagates the teardown error before writing its JSON report. Completed pass, failure and timeout evidence disappears; child failure/timeout exit codes are replaced by an uncaught exception. This is a finite fault-injection finding, not a claim that native Windows has reproduced the trigger.
findings.requested_change: Handle the isolated environment cleanup failure separately from command execution, preserve completed command results and existing nonzero child/timeout code, turn otherwise-successful cleanup failure into nonzero failed status, and publish an explicit cleanup diagnostic through the requested report when its destination is writable.

paths.review_scope: Additional CI4 teardown/report-publication finding only. Prior CI1/CI2/CI3 closure remains intact. No other previously approved source behavior is reopened.

findings.impact: Always-uploaded machine reports can be missing after the dependent runner exits during environment teardown.

independent_execution.method: Compile exact git-show runner module. Patch commands_for to run one actual finite synthetic Python child. Subclass the real TemporaryDirectory: __exit__ first performs real successful cleanup, then raises PermissionError("synthetic environment cleanup denied"). Keep requested reports in a separate writable temporary directory. Invoke main with --suite unit --timeout1 and catch the injected error only in the diagnostic driver.

limitations: No native Windows cleanup error, live request or broad suite was exercised. The injected cleanup error isolates a valid exception path without leaving processes or temporary environments behind.
The report destination was writable in every probe. Report publication cannot be promised when that destination itself fails; that is outside this finding.
Prior CI1/CI2/CI3 source and focused-test closure is retained. Native cross-platform acceptance remains unverified.
Only a new review artifact is authored here; the offline runner owner is responsible for the narrow implementation and regression fix.
